content.text: This approach of counting listitems is unreliable since not all items follow a fixed pattern and it's easy to miscount, plus the list is cut off (need to check more further pages). A much more reliable approach: use grep to find "cite_ref-" or "cite_note-" numbering directly in the raw page, or navigate directly to the anchor via URL fragment. Wikipedia reference numbers do correspond to cite_note-N for the plain numbered ones, but named refs break the sequence. Let me instead check the actual rendered page HTML by looking for the ol counter — better to navigate to the reference list and use the browser's rendered numbering by jumping directly to `#cite_note-275`.

content.text: This approach of counting listitems is unreliable since not all items follow a fixed pattern and it's easy to miscount, plus the list is cut off (need to check more further pages). A much more reliable approach: use grep to find "cite_ref-" or "cite_note-" numbering directly in the raw page, or navigate directly to the anchor via URL fragment. Wikipedia reference numbers do correspond to cite_note-N for the plain numbered ones, but named refs break the sequence. Let me instead check the actual rendered page HTML by looking for the ol counter — better to navigate to the reference list and use the browser's rendered numbering by jumping directly to `#cite_note-275`.

content.text: This approach of counting listitems is unreliable since not all items follow a fixed pattern and it's easy to miscount, plus the list is cut off (need to check more further pages). A much more reliable approach: use grep to find "cite_ref-" or "cite_note-" numbering directly in the raw page, or navigate directly to the anchor via URL fragment. Wikipedia reference numbers do correspond to cite_note-N for the plain numbered ones, but named refs break the sequence. Let me instead check the actual rendered page HTML by looking for the ol counter — better to navigate to the reference list and use the browser's rendered numbering by jumping directly to `#cite_note-275`.

content.text: This approach of counting listitems is unreliable since not all items follow a fixed pattern and it's easy to miscount, plus the list is cut off (need to check more further pages). A much more reliable approach: use grep to find "cite_ref-" or "cite_note-" numbering directly in the raw page, or navigate directly to the anchor via URL fragment. Wikipedia reference numbers do correspond to cite_note-N for the plain numbered ones, but named refs break the sequence. Let me instead check the actual rendered page HTML by looking for the ol counter — better to navigate to the reference list and use the browser's rendered numbering by jumping directly to `#cite_note-275`.
